title: BITS Hyderabad students pitch Army a radio at 1/5th the import price

slides.head: BITS Hyderabad students pitch Army a radio at 1/5th the import price
What happened
slides.body: Krath Control pairs with a soldier's phone and links to nearby radios in an encrypted mesh that reroutes if one node drops out.

slides.head: Why it matters
slides.body: Conventional voice radios don't show locations, and imported live-map systems cost several times more and are closed systems, the founders say.

slides.head: Did you know
slides.body: The radio weighs under 180 grams and needs no tower, satellite or SIM.

slides.head: What to watch
slides.body: Whether the upgraded radio, due in two to three months, clears a second Army assessment. Ask: What does an Army trial need to see before it buys an Indian device?

captions.instagram:
BITS Hyderabad students pitch Army a radio at 1/5th the import price

Krathveil, a startup by two 20-year-old BITS Pilani Hyderabad students, has built Krath Control, a sub-180 g radio that links soldiers over an encrypted mesh without towers, satellites or SIM cards. Two Army units have assessed it.

Why it matters: Conventional voice radios don't show locations, and imported live-map systems cost several times more and are closed systems, the founders say.

Source: Times of India. Image: Times of India
